fact: The first farmed wheats were einkorn and emmer. Bread wheat came later, when emmer crossed with a wild grass.
Barley was one of the first crops ever grown, and some of the earliest beer was made from it.
Lentils were one of the “founder crops” that started farming in the Middle East.
Wild chickpeas still grow in a small area of southeast Turkey.
Gregor Mendel used peas to discover how traits are inherited.

region: the Levant (around today’s Israel, Lebanon and Syria)
fact: Some olive trees still producing fruit are thought to be over 2,000 years old.
Date palms are either male or female, and growers pollinate the females by hand.
Some of the oldest traces of wine, about 8,000 years old, come from pottery jars in Georgia.
Flax gives both linseed oil and linen, one of the oldest fabrics.
More than half the people on Earth eat rice as their main food.
Its wild ancestor is a thin vine with tiny seeds that still grows in East Asia.
Green, black, white and oolong tea all come from this one plant, just processed differently.
Its Latin name means “Persian plum” because Europeans first got peaches from Persia.
The sweet orange is a cross between a pomelo and a mandarin.
Despite the name, buckwheat isn’t a wheat or even a grass. It’s related to rhubarb.
Hemp was grown for rope and cloth long before paper was invented, which it was also used for.
Wild apple forests still grow near Almaty, a city named after the Kazakh word for apple.
The first farmed carrots were purple and yellow. Orange ones became common much later.
Onions were found in the eye sockets of the mummy of Pharaoh Ramesses IV.
The mango is the national fruit of India, Pakistan and the Philippines.
Peppercorns were so valuable they were found stuffed in the nostrils of the mummy of Ramesses II.

region: the foothills of the Himalayas, India
fact: Its wild relatives in India have bitter, spiny fruits.
“Open sesame” may come from the way ripe pods suddenly burst open.
Bananas we eat are seedless, so new plants are grown from cuttings.
Sugarcane is the world’s biggest crop by weight.
Coffee grows wild in Ethiopia’s forests. The first coffee farms and coffee houses were in Yemen.
Sorghum survives droughts that would kill maize.
Teff is used to make injera, Ethiopia’s spongy flatbread.
A wild watermelon from Sudan with sweet red flesh is the closest relative of the farmed one.
Palm oil is in about half of all packaged products in supermarkets.
Nigeria grows about two thirds of the world’s yams.
Maize comes from teosinte, a wild grass with tiny cobs only a few centimetres long.
Maize, beans and squash were grown together as the “three sisters”.
Squash seeds from a cave in Oaxaca are some of the oldest crop remains in the Americas.
Chilies only reached Asia in the 1500s, so Thai and Indian food had no chilies before then.
Its big seed may have been spread by giant ground sloths that are now extinct.
Outside Mexico, vanilla flowers have to be pollinated by hand, one at a time.
Tequila can only legally come from Jalisco and a few nearby areas.
Upland cotton from Mexico makes up about 90% of the cotton grown today.
It’s one of very few major crops first farmed in what is now the United States.
Blueberries were tamed only in the early 1900s, by a botanist and a farmer’s daughter in New Jersey.
The oldest traces of cacao use were found in pottery from southern Ecuador.
Andean farmers still grow thousands of potato varieties.
Quinoa is related to spinach and beets, not to grasses like wheat.
Peanut flowers bloom above ground, then the stalk bends down and pushes the pod into the soil.
Raw cassava contains cyanide, so it has to be soaked, cooked or fermented first.
Each pineapple is made of many small fruits fused together.
The first farmed tomatoes were small, from Ecuador and Peru. The big tomatoes we know were developed later in Mexico.

region: Central America and northern South America
fact: Sweet potatoes reached Polynesia before Europeans did. How they crossed the Pacific is still debated.
It takes about 150 flowers to make one gram of saffron.
Cabbage, broccoli, kale, cauliflower and Brussels sprouts are all the same species.
Sugar beet was bred in the 1700s; it now gives about a fifth of the world’s sugar.
The garden strawberry is a 1700s cross between a Chilean and a North American strawberry, made in France.
